item.title: 日本免稅新制「先付後退」上路！黃牛狂買名牌逃漏稅，竟要全體觀光客買單？【TODAY 看世界】
item.itunes:title: 日本免稅新制「先付後退」上路！黃牛狂買名牌逃漏稅，竟要全體觀光客買單？【TODAY 看世界】
item.itunes:author: TODAY 看世界

值得閱讀的理由

  • 掌握日本免稅新制的退款流程，避免因托運順序或物品缺漏而拿不到退款。
  • 了解制度變更的背景，包括免稅商品遭轉售、商家補繳稅款等問題。
  • 看懂退款手續費、機場查驗與商家應對等實際影響，為赴日購物做好準備。

摘要

免稅制度為何改變

范姬妃指出，日本自11月1日起採行新的免稅制度：旅客結帳時先支付含稅價格，離境時再經海關確認商品確實帶出日本，才能申請退稅；退款方式與金額則依商店及服務商而異，可能還會扣除手續費。過去旅客在結帳時就能直接免稅，如今則須多走幾個步驟。

日本免稅政策可追溯至1952年，後來隨消費稅制度發展，逐步擴大適用商品範圍，並降低消費門檻。舊制下，旅客同一天在同一家店消費滿5,000日圓，通常就能享有10%的免稅優惠。日本觀光消費近年屢創新高，外國旅客去年消費約達1.9兆新台幣，其中購物支出超過5,300億元，占三成左右。

新制要堵住舊制漏洞

舊制先行免稅，仰賴旅客會把商品帶出境的假設，但有人利用制度漏洞，在日本境內轉售免稅商品牟利。影片舉例，海關曾查獲旅客大量購買名錶與名牌包後轉賣，也有大量購買蘋果產品的案例，導致企業遭追繳巨額稅款；多家零售商也曾因不合規的免稅交易被要求補稅。

過去部分商店會以封條包裝免稅商品，海關若發現封條遭拆，便可要求旅客補繳稅款；但旅客若無力付款，追討並不容易。范姬妃說，新制的核心是先收取含稅價格，確認商品符合規定後再退款，把未能追回稅款的風險從政府轉移出去。

旅客申請退稅的流程與三個陷阱

購物時仍須出示護照，並依商店指示登記退款資料，可能透過信用卡、銀行轉帳或部分機場的現金方式領取。旅客須在購買後90天內離境，並完成海關查驗。第一個關鍵是先查驗、再托運：旅客可在免稅查驗設備掃描護照，若系統要求檢查行李，就必須讓海關查看；若商品已先托運，海關便無法確認，退款也可能失敗。

第二，收據所列商品都必須隨身帶出境；若同一筆交易中有一件商品缺少，整筆交易的免稅資格都可能失效。因此，打算在日本送人或分送的商品，最好分開結帳。電器等商品即使在日本拆封使用，只要離境時仍帶在身上，仍可符合免稅條件。第三，退款可能扣除服務費：例如稅前消費30,000日圓，原可退3,000日圓，但實際退款會因商店與退款業者的費用而減少；目前不少業者收取約1%至3%的費用。

新制也有便利之處，例如店員不必再把商品裝入特定封袋，單店過去50萬日圓的免稅購物上限也已取消。官方表示，全國36處機場與港口設有約200台查驗設備，掃描護照只需數秒，但旅客仍應為額外檢查預留時間。成田、羽田與關西等主要機場也可透過專用Wi-Fi使用Visit Japan Web辦理確認。

商家適應與各方觀點

新制上路前，受訪免稅商店經理中只有約兩成表示已完全準備妥當。商家對未來業績看法不一：有人擔心旅客看到先付含稅價格後會降低購物意願，也有人看好免稅銷售增加。若退款金額不高，銀行轉帳或系統費用甚至可能吃掉一大部分退款；部分公司因此嘗試在市區先辦理退款，但旅客須登記信用卡，若未完成離境查驗，款項會再從卡片扣回。

影片提到，韓國提供多種免稅方式；歐盟不少國家則與日本新制相似，先支付含稅價格，再於機場辦理退款。因此，日本的新制並非前所未有，只是旅客已習慣舊制，需要時間適應。從日本調整住宿稅、出境稅及免稅制度來看，如何兼顧吸引觀光消費、防止制度遭濫用，以及釐清觀光成本由誰負擔，都是日益重要的課題。

范姬妃的購物習慣與結語

范姬妃分享，自己旅行時通常只買需要的東西，不太會因價格而改變決定，也常懶得特地辦退稅；但和台灣朋友同行後，她才發現大家很熟悉退稅流程，跟著辦理後，退款通常足以在機場吃一碗拉麵。最後，她邀請觀眾分享是否常在旅行時購物、是否會申請退稅，以及認為日本新制是否合理、會不會因此減少消費。

================================================

Many people plan their Japan trips by calculating exchange rates and tax-free savings, but that strategy now needs an update. Starting November 1st, Japan’s new tax-free system requires you to pay the tax-included price upfront. You must then have customs verify the items upon departure to claim a refund, which may also incur a processing fee. Savings that were once instant at checkout now require extra steps, and. the final refund amount depends on the store and method used. Why is Japan making this change? What should you know about tax refunds for your next trip to avoid unnecessary losses? Hello everyone, I’m Fan Ji-fei. Welcome to Fan-Kan Incident. First, let’s explain what this tax is. Consumption tax is meant for goods used within Japan. Since tourists take these items back to.

their home countries, they shouldn't have to pay it, hence the exemption. Japan's tax-free policy dates back to 1952. While there was no consumption tax then, luxury goods like jewelry and furs were taxed; tourists were exempt. When the consumption tax was introduced in 1989, the system remained. The system has been revised seven times , eventually including consumables like. cosmetics and food, and lowering the minimum spend threshold to 5,000 yen. The old system was simple: spend 5,000 yen—about 1,040 NTD—at one store in a day to get a 10%tax exemption, either deducted at checkout or refunded at a counter. Japan has become a major Asian tourism hub. According to the Japan Tourism Agency, foreign tourist spending on food,.

lodging, and shopping hit a record high of about 1.9 trillion NTD last year. Tourism is now Japan's second-largest export industry after automobiles. Of that 1.9 trillion, over 530 billion NTD was spent on shopping, accounting for 30%of the total. So, why the change ? The previous system relied on the honor system, assuming that if you met the tourist criteria, you intended to take the goods home. However, many exploited this loophole by reselling tax-free goods within Japan for a profit. By the time authorities realized the items hadn't left the country, it was too late to collect the tax. Many shops have suffered greatly from this. For instance, in 2022, Japanese customs found nine people who bought luxury watches and bags worth NT $ 680 million, evading over NT $ 70 million in taxes through duty-free loopholes and reselling them for a profit. Even more absurdly, some bought hundreds of Apple products tax-free in.

2022. Apple Japan ended up footing the bill, hit with NT $ 2.7 billion in back taxes by the Tokyo Regional Taxation Bureau. That same year, Apple Japan stopped offering duty-free services. Meanwhile, stores like Don Quijote, Nishimatsuya, and the drugstore chain Matsumoto Kiyoshi have also been hit with massive back tax bills by the tax authorities for selling duty-free goods to ineligible customers. Under the old system, to prevent tourists from using duty-free items, many drugstores and shops would seal goods in red adhesive. plastic bags that would show clear signs of tampering if opened. While customs could easily tell if the seal was broken upon departure and demand payment on the spot, they couldn't hold travelers if they claimed to have no money, leaving them with no choice but to issue a tax debt notice. According to Kyodo News, in 2022 alone, authorities failed to recover over NT $ 380 million in unpaid taxes from major duty-free offenders. In short, the old system granted tax exemptions upfront and chased you for the money if you were caught.

The new system charges you first, and only refunds you once you’ve proven you followed the rules, shifting the risk away from the Japanese government. So. For those of us who love traveling to Japan, what exactly changes? First, the process: you still show your passport at checkout. Following the shop's instructions, you register your refund details to receive the money via credit card, bank transfer, or cash at some airports. After purchasing, you must depart within 90 days and complete the customs verification at the airport. to receive your refund. The process sounds simple, but there are three common pitfalls. First is the timing: you must complete the tax refund procedure before checking your luggage. Scan your passport at the duty-free kiosk; a green light means you’re cleared to check your bags and board the flight. A red light means you must let customs inspect your bags. If you check your luggage immediately upon arrival at the airport, customs cannot verify your goods, and you won’t get your refund. Second, you must have all items on the receipt with you.

Duty-free data is sent to customs online , so you don't necessarily need to keep paper receipts. However, if any single item from a receipt is missing, the tax exemption for the entire transaction is voided. So, if you buy souvenirs to give away or distribute while still in Japan, be sure to pay for those items in separate transactions. Conversely, for items like hair dryers or electric appliances, if you open and use them in Japan, as long as you carry them with you when leaving the country, you are still eligible for. the tax exemption. Third is the service fee. If you buy items worth 30,000 yen before tax, you should get a 3,000 yen refund, but after deducting the service fee, you'll actually get back a bit less . Whether a tax refund fee is charged and how much depends on the store and their refund provider; currently, most store service fees are around 1%to 3%of the purchase amount. Of course, there are benefits to this, such as not having to wait for store staff to pack items in special packaging , which also lightens the burden on stores.

The previous 500,000 yen limit for tax-free purchases at a single store has also been abolished. Many people are worried about major congestion at airports. Officials say there are about 200 tax exemption confirmation kiosks at 36 airports and ports nationwide, and scanning a passport to see the results only takes a few seconds, though extra time should be reserved for further checks. At major airports like Narita, Haneda, and Kansai, you can connect to the dedicated Wi-Fi and use your phone to access the Visit Japan Web page, saving. you the time of going to a kiosk and doing it yourself on your phone. No. It's not just tourists still figuring out how to get refunds; Japanese shops are also still adapting. A tax-free service provider surveyed 104 duty-free shop managers in October, and at that time, only about 20%were fully prepared. Opinions on business prospects for the next three months are mixed; over 40%fear tax-free sales will decline , while nearly 60%believe they will.

increase. Whether this new system is a hassle or an opportunity, shops are still taking a "wait and see" approach. Shops worried about a downturn fear a change in tourist shopping psychology. Previously, if an item was 100,000 yen tax-free, you paid 100,000. Now you pay 110,000 upfront; while the money is eventually refunded, the feeling of paying more is different, and shops face cost pressures too. Japanese media point out that if the refund is only 500 yen, bank transfer and system fees could eat up more than half of it. Beyond costs,. shops also have to find ways to maintain the customer's desire to shop. Some companies now offer downtown tax refund services, giving you the refund in shopping districts so you don't have to wait until departure. However, you must register a credit card, and if you fail to complete customs verification, they will charge the amount back to your card . Experts say that if you look at the current duty-free policy alongside recent adjustments to accommodation and departure taxes, it is clear that Japan wants tourists to visit and spend more.

However, how to prevent abuse of the system and who bears the costs brought by tourism are issues that increasingly need to be clarified. Looking at other countries, South Korea maintains a variety of tax-free methods; some allow direct purchases at duty-free prices in stores, while others, like the new Japanese system, require a post-purchase refund. EU countries are similar to Japan, where you must first pay the tax-included price and process the refund at the airport, with the tax amount returned to you later. Therefore , Japan's new system is not a. groundbreaking innovation, as many countries have done this for years. It is just that people were too accustomed to the old tax-free method, so the new system will inevitably have an adjustment period. I don't buy much when I travel. I only buy things because I need them, rarely because I want them, but once I decide to buy, I don't really care about the price. Since I need the items, I'm often too lazy to even bother with the tax refund process. My ex-husband, Rob, has habits very similar to mine. It wasn't until I traveled with friends from Taiwan that I realized how well everyone understands the tax refund.

process! Since I went along with them, I ended up processing the refund as well. It actually helps a bit, usually enough to have a bowl of ramen at the airport. So, do you always buy things when you travel? Do you always get a tax refund when you buy things? Do you think Japan's change is reasonable? Will you buy less because of this? Leave a comment and tell me. If you like this show, please share it with more people. You can subscribe to our official LINE account. It sends a daily package of important news and this program directly to your phone. In case you miss it, our channel contains all our reports. Follow "World" as we select one international topic for you every day.

However, many exploited this loophole by reselling tax-free goods within Japan for a profit. By the time authorities realized the items hadn't left the country, it was too late to collect the tax. Many shops have suffered greatly from this. For instance, in 2022, Japanese customs found nine people who bought luxury watches and bags worth NT $ 680 million, evading over NT $ 70 million in taxes through duty-free loopholes and reselling them for a profit. Even more absurdly, some bought hundreds of Apple products tax-free in.

2022. Apple Japan ended up footing the bill, hit with NT $ 2.7 billion in back taxes by the Tokyo Regional Taxation Bureau. That same year, Apple Japan stopped offering duty-free services. Meanwhile, stores like Don Quijote, Nishimatsuya, and the drugstore chain Matsumoto Kiyoshi have also been hit with massive back tax bills by the tax authorities for selling duty-free goods to ineligible customers. Under the old system, to prevent tourists from using duty-free items, many drugstores and shops would seal goods in red adhesive. plastic bags that would show clear signs of tampering if opened. While customs could easily tell if the seal was broken upon departure and demand payment on the spot, they couldn't hold travelers if they claimed to have no money, leaving them with no choice but to issue a tax debt notice. According to Kyodo News, in 2022 alone, authorities failed to recover over NT $ 380 million in unpaid taxes from major duty-free offenders. In short, the old system granted tax exemptions upfront and chased you for the money if you were caught.

The new system charges you first, and only refunds you once you’ve proven you followed the rules, shifting the risk away from the Japanese government. So. For those of us who love traveling to Japan, what exactly changes? First, the process: you still show your passport at checkout. Following the shop's instructions, you register your refund details to receive the money via credit card, bank transfer, or cash at some airports. After purchasing, you must depart within 90 days and complete the customs verification at the airport. to receive your refund. The process sounds simple, but there are three common pitfalls. First is the timing: you must complete the tax refund procedure before checking your luggage. Scan your passport at the duty-free kiosk; a green light means you’re cleared to check your bags and board the flight. A red light means you must let customs inspect your bags. If you check your luggage immediately upon arrival at the airport, customs cannot verify your goods, and you won’t get your refund. Second, you must have all items on the receipt with you.

Duty-free data is sent to customs online , so you don't necessarily need to keep paper receipts. However, if any single item from a receipt is missing, the tax exemption for the entire transaction is voided. So, if you buy souvenirs to give away or distribute while still in Japan, be sure to pay for those items in separate transactions. Conversely, for items like hair dryers or electric appliances, if you open and use them in Japan, as long as you carry them with you when leaving the country, you are still eligible for. the tax exemption. Third is the service fee. If you buy items worth 30,000 yen before tax, you should get a 3,000 yen refund, but after deducting the service fee, you'll actually get back a bit less . Whether a tax refund fee is charged and how much depends on the store and their refund provider; currently, most store service fees are around 1%to 3%of the purchase amount. Of course, there are benefits to this, such as not having to wait for store staff to pack items in special packaging , which also lightens the burden on stores.

The previous 500,000 yen limit for tax-free purchases at a single store has also been abolished. Many people are worried about major congestion at airports. Officials say there are about 200 tax exemption confirmation kiosks at 36 airports and ports nationwide, and scanning a passport to see the results only takes a few seconds, though extra time should be reserved for further checks. At major airports like Narita, Haneda, and Kansai, you can connect to the dedicated Wi-Fi and use your phone to access the Visit Japan Web page, saving. you the time of going to a kiosk and doing it yourself on your phone. No. It's not just tourists still figuring out how to get refunds; Japanese shops are also still adapting. A tax-free service provider surveyed 104 duty-free shop managers in October, and at that time, only about 20%were fully prepared. Opinions on business prospects for the next three months are mixed; over 40%fear tax-free sales will decline , while nearly 60%believe they will.

increase. Whether this new system is a hassle or an opportunity, shops are still taking a "wait and see" approach. Shops worried about a downturn fear a change in tourist shopping psychology. Previously, if an item was 100,000 yen tax-free, you paid 100,000. Now you pay 110,000 upfront; while the money is eventually refunded, the feeling of paying more is different, and shops face cost pressures too. Japanese media point out that if the refund is only 500 yen, bank transfer and system fees could eat up more than half of it. Beyond costs,. shops also have to find ways to maintain the customer's desire to shop. Some companies now offer downtown tax refund services, giving you the refund in shopping districts so you don't have to wait until departure. However, you must register a credit card, and if you fail to complete customs verification, they will charge the amount back to your card . process! Since I went along with them, I ended up processing the refund as well. It actually helps a bit, usually enough to have a bowl of ramen at the airport. 值得閱讀的理由

  • 掌握日本免稅新制的退款流程，避免因托運順序或物品缺漏而拿不到退款。
  • 了解制度變更的背景，包括免稅商品遭轉售、商家補繳稅款等問題。
  • 看懂退款手續費、機場查驗與商家應對等實際影響，為赴日購物做好準備。

摘要

免稅制度為何改變

范姬妃指出，日本自11月1日起採行新的免稅制度：旅客結帳時先支付含稅價格，離境時再經海關確認商品確實帶出日本，才能申請退稅；退款方式與金額則依商店及服務商而異，可能還會扣除手續費。過去旅客在結帳時就能直接免稅，如今則須多走幾個步驟。

日本免稅政策可追溯至1952年，後來隨消費稅制度發展，逐步擴大適用商品範圍，並降低消費門檻。舊制下，旅客同一天在同一家店消費滿5,000日圓，通常就能享有10%的免稅優惠。日本觀光消費近年屢創新高，外國旅客去年消費約達1.9兆新台幣，其中購物支出超過5,300億元，占三成左右。

新制要堵住舊制漏洞

舊制先行免稅，仰賴旅客會把商品帶出境的假設，但有人利用制度漏洞，在日本境內轉售免稅商品牟利。影片舉例，海關曾查獲旅客大量購買名錶與名牌包後轉賣，也有大量購買蘋果產品的案例，導致企業遭追繳巨額稅款；多家零售商也曾因不合規的免稅交易被要求補稅。

過去部分商店會以封條包裝免稅商品，海關若發現封條遭拆，便可要求旅客補繳稅款；但旅客若無力付款，追討並不容易。范姬妃說，新制的核心是先收取含稅價格，確認商品符合規定後再退款，把未能追回稅款的風險從政府轉移出去。

旅客申請退稅的流程與三個陷阱

購物時仍須出示護照，並依商店指示登記退款資料，可能透過信用卡、銀行轉帳或部分機場的現金方式領取。旅客須在購買後90天內離境，並完成海關查驗。第一個關鍵是先查驗、再托運：旅客可在免稅查驗設備掃描護照，若系統要求檢查行李，就必須讓海關查看；若商品已先托運，海關便無法確認，退款也可能失敗。

第二，收據所列商品都必須隨身帶出境；若同一筆交易中有一件商品缺少，整筆交易的免稅資格都可能失效。因此，打算在日本送人或分送的商品，最好分開結帳。電器等商品即使在日本拆封使用，只要離境時仍帶在身上，仍可符合免稅條件。第三，退款可能扣除服務費：例如稅前消費30,000日圓，原可退3,000日圓，但實際退款會因商店與退款業者的費用而減少；目前不少業者收取約1%至3%的費用。

新制也有便利之處，例如店員不必再把商品裝入特定封袋，單店過去50萬日圓的免稅購物上限也已取消。官方表示，全國36處機場與港口設有約200台查驗設備，掃描護照只需數秒，但旅客仍應為額外檢查預留時間。成田、羽田與關西等主要機場也可透過專用Wi-Fi使用Visit Japan Web辦理確認。

商家適應與各方觀點

新制上路前，受訪免稅商店經理中只有約兩成表示已完全準備妥當。商家對未來業績看法不一：有人擔心旅客看到先付含稅價格後會降低購物意願，也有人看好免稅銷售增加。若退款金額不高，銀行轉帳或系統費用甚至可能吃掉一大部分退款；部分公司因此嘗試在市區先辦理退款，但旅客須登記信用卡，若未完成離境查驗，款項會再從卡片扣回。

影片提到，韓國提供多種免稅方式；歐盟不少國家則與日本新制相似，先支付含稅價格，再於機場辦理退款。因此，日本的新制並非前所未有，只是旅客已習慣舊制，需要時間適應。從日本調整住宿稅、出境稅及免稅制度來看，如何兼顧吸引觀光消費、防止制度遭濫用，以及釐清觀光成本由誰負擔，都是日益重要的課題。

范姬妃的購物習慣與結語

范姬妃分享，自己旅行時通常只買需要的東西，不太會因價格而改變決定，也常懶得特地辦退稅；但和台灣朋友同行後，她才發現大家很熟悉退稅流程，跟著辦理後，退款通常足以在機場吃一碗拉麵。最後，她邀請觀眾分享是否常在旅行時購物、是否會申請退稅，以及認為日本新制是否合理、會不會因此減少消費。

值得閱讀的理由

  • 掌握輝達執行長黃仁勳爆發婚外情及捲入中國間諜風波的始末，了解其對科技界與輝達營運的深遠震盪。
  • 剖析美中科技禁令下的「境外算力」監管漏洞，理解中國如何透過東南亞資料中心迂迴獲取關鍵 AI 運算資源。
  • 洞悉華府政壇對該事件的國安角力反應、法案收緊趨勢，以及給予台灣企業與政府的防諜警示。

摘要

桃色風波升級：黃仁勳承認婚外情與中國間諜疑雲

輝達執行長黃仁勳突向全公司發送內部信坦承婚外情，外遇對象為中國籍女子黃樂。美國媒體隨後披露，美國情報界懷疑黃樂已被中國國家安全部招募，涉嫌藉由親密關係蒐集先進科技情報。輝達因此展開內部獨立調查，黃仁勳亦面臨國會質詢壓力，市場擔憂先進 AI 技術與商業機密外洩，導致輝達股價震盪並引發全球高度關注。

採購案引發監聽：揭開境外算力的防堵漏洞

此起事件源自新加坡公司 Megaspeed 短期內斥資巨額採購輝達設備送往馬來西亞，美方因懷疑晶片最終轉運至中國而展開監聽，意外揭露任職該公司高層的黃樂與黃仁勳交往甚密。這場風暴也徹底暴露了美方管制的「境外算力」漏洞，顯示中國企業即使不直接進口高階晶片，也能透過租用東南亞等第三地資料中心規避限制，大幅增加終端追查與防堵的難度。

華府政治角力、個人形象重挫與防諜警訊

美國國會介入並要求黃仁勳出席閉門簡報，鷹派勢力更藉機要求暫停對中出口晶片並推動法案防堵漏洞。雖然川普政府知悉情資後依然公開力挺，且因缺乏合適接班人使黃仁勳短期內暫無去職危機，但其長年塑造的顧家形象已遭受重擊。作者提醒，雖然目前無直接洩密證據，但該案凸顯了中國情報滲透手段的無孔不入，台灣與全球高科技產業及政府機構皆應強化資安戒心與防諜規範。

這場風波讓黃仁勳面臨輝達的獨立調查，還被國會要求出席閉門簡報，事件會不會進一步擴大，影響美國的科技管制，甚至動搖黃仁勳在華府的影響力？黃仁勳會因此失去輝達董座的位子嗎？
